item.text:
**3B.5 Research Note: Olaf Scholz in 2024**

**Assessment:** The 2024 record is mostly **lawful, bounded, and oversight-oriented**. Scholz and his government used security tools for deterrence, investigation, and prevention, not for mass intimidation or collective punishment. The main counterweight is that Germany’s intelligence-surveillance law was still partly unconstitutional in late 2024, which shows a real oversight deficit at the system level.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Scholz: Germany’s security authorities had prepared for a high-risk summer** | Bundesregierung | 6 Jun 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/suche/scholz-sicherheitslage-2291096 | Scholz said the state would protect police, back investigations, and punish killings and attacks “with the full force of the law.” He also said the Generalbundesanwalt had taken over the case, which points to formal legal process rather than arbitrary punishment. | **3B.5**, also **3B.2**, **3B.1** |
| **Germany’s first National Security Strategy** | Bundesregierung | 14 Jun 2023, operative in 2024 | https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-en/aktuelles/national-security-strategy-2196356 | The strategy is explicitly a “systematic overall approach” covering diplomacy, police, fire brigades, civil protection, cyber security, supply-chain resilience, and pandemic prevention. That is a broad, preventive security framework rather than an intimidation tool. | **3B.5** |
| **Joint press release on the Federal Government report evaluating Bundeswehr missions abroad** | Federal Foreign Office / Federal Ministry of Defence | 26 Jun 2024 | https://www.auswaertiges-amt.de/en/newsroom/news/2664958-2664958 | The government conducted its first overarching evaluation of ongoing Bundeswehr missions abroad using uniform criteria and identified improvement needs, including better civilian-military coordination. This is evidence of review and administrative learning, not unreviewed coercion. | **3B.5**, also **3B.4** |
| **The Federal Intelligence Service’s powers to conduct strategic surveillance... are unconstitutional in part** | Bundesverfassungsgericht | 8 Nov 2024 | https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Pressemitteilungen/EN/2024/bvg24-093.html | The Constitutional Court said BND cyber-surveillance powers were only partly constitutional and that independent oversight under the Article 10 Committee was inadequate. This is the strongest counterweight: Germany had an overbroad surveillance framework and weak oversight, even if that was a legal-structural defect rather than proof of personal abuse by Scholz. | **3B.5** |
| **Verfassungsfeinde in Sicherheitsbehörden schnell erkennen und bekämpfen** | Bundesamt für Verfassungsschutz / BMI | 2024 press release | https://www.verfassungsschutz.de/SharedDocs/pressemitteilungen/DE/2024/pressemitteilung-2024-rechtsextremisten-in-sicherheitsbehoerden.html | The security-authority report says 436 disciplinary or labor-law proceedings were initiated against personnel with extremist indicators, and the new federal disciplinary law speeds removal of abusive actors. This supports a picture of targeted discipline and internal control, not tolerance of abuse. | **3B.5**, also **3B.2** |
| **Germany cannot accept spying, says Scholz after suspected China spy arrested** | Reuters / Investing.com | 24 Apr 2024 | https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/germany-cannot-accept-spying-says-scholz-after-suspected-china-spy-arrested-3451540 | Scholz said Germany would not accept foreign spying and wanted those responsible put on trial, while avoiding prejudgment during legal proceedings. That is due-process language, not administrative intimidation. | **3B.5**, also **3B.4** |

**Bottom line**
- Strong evidence points to **narrow, law-based use** of security powers: investigation, prosecution, discipline, preventive planning, and post-mission review.
- The main negative item is the **BVerfG ruling on BND surveillance**, which shows that some security powers remained too broad and oversight was not yet sufficient.
- I found **no reliable evidence** that Scholz used emergency powers, surveillance, or anti-terror controls for collective punishment or intimidation in 2024.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a 2024 case where Scholz personally used emergency powers in a way that resembled authoritarian control.
- Germany in 2024 looks more like a constitutional-security state with some overbroad surveillance problems than a leader using security law for repression.
